PythonExport.Name: ElementAppearancePy

Documentation.UserDocu:
What the elements of an object's shape look like, held by the object.
A view of the property it was read from, not a copy: a write to it changes the object and is one step to undo.
An element is named as the shape counts it ('Face3'), by its mapped name, or by its number as a list of faces counts it (2). 'Face', 'Edge' and 'Vertex' are the object's own look, which every element has that states nothing.
ea = obj.ElementAppearance ea['Face3'] = material # all of it is the face's own ea['Face3'] = (1.0, 0.0, 0.0) # its colour; the rest follows the object ea[2] # the same face, as it is drawn del ea['Face3'] # back to the object's look ea.Face = material # the object's own look
A look is held by the element's name where the shape has a mapped name for it, and follows the element through a recompute; where the shape has none it is held by the number.
keys() -> list: the elements something is stated of, the named ones first.
items() -> list of (name, Material): what is stated, each as it is drawn.

update(dict) -> None: every entry written, as one change.
A key is an element as indexing takes it; a value a Material or a colour.

setLook(element, material, own=None) -> None
Give an element a look. own names the fields that are the element's own, as App.Material spells them -- ('DiffuseColor', 'Shininess') -- and the rest follow the object; left out, all of the material is the element's.
setColor(element, color) -> None: the colour alone; the rest follows the object.
own(element) -> tuple: the fields the element states, empty if it states nothing.
isNamed(element) -> bool: whether its look is held by its name and not its number.
remove(element) -> bool: back to the object's look; False if nothing was stated of it.
clear() -> None: nothing stated, the object's own look included.
The object's own look: every face's that states nothing.
